You will need an electric arc welder or a MIG welder.

I was trying to find a cheap TIG kit but it looks like Stick is still the cheapest. You said Home Depot so I'll just go with that. Here is a 120 volt stick welder for $100. You'll still need a hood also but they have cheap-0 kits that should get you through. Angle is fine just be sure to clean the scale off around your weld paths.

What does your comment about keeping the connections as clean as possible? Is that for the printer to travel over? If so you could always grind your weld paths back down to flush. Beveling the weldments and filling the path back flush will keep it solid. As far as keeping it straight you'll just need to counter the draw from a weld. Good clamping will mitigate draw some.

It's going to be more than $60 to get started welding but on the plus side you'll be able to weld which seems more versatile than oxy. I'm more of a TIG/MIG person than SMAW so I won't be much help there. Good luck and have fun and always have good ventilation!

If I assume you need 1/8" thick angle iron or thinner, there are many ways to assemble you frame.

Brazing it with bronze or silver (silver is more expensive but flows way better at lower temps) is a good option, can get away with a cheap MAPP torch kit or even better oxy-fuel (propane or acetylene). Requires light chamfers & clean, tight fitting joint. Don't wear sandles !

A cheap arc welder with 3/32" dia. 7018 rod at around 65-70 amps DC+ (amp it up 10-15% if using AC current), chamfers are optional depending on the finishing requirements.

Or find a fellow hobbyist near you with a mig or tig welder (not worth investing in these welders if it's just for occasional use) who can give you a hand.

Ranger 7 was the first American space probe to successfully transmit close images of the lunar surface back to Earth. Launched on July 28, 1964, Ranger 7 was designed to achieve a lunar-impact trajectory and to transmit high-resolution photographs of the lunar surface during the final minutes of flight up to impact. Ranger 7 transmitted over 4,300 photographs during the final 17 minutes of its flight. The velocity at impact was 1.62 miles per second, and the performance of the spacecraft exceeded hopes. No other experiments were carried on the spacecraft.
